thread.title: Live by the FAANG Stocks, and Die With Them

author: Evie Liu
title: Live by the FAANG Stocks, and Die With Them
text:
By Evie Liu Updated July 31, 2018 3:39 p.m. ET If you live by the FAANGs, you die by the FAANGs—and the Nasdaq 100 has been more tied to Facebook (FB), Apple (AAPL), Amazon.com (AMZN), Netflix (NFLX), and Alphabet (GOOGL) than ever.
Facebook tumbled 19% last Thursday following its disappointing second-quarter earnings, and the pain quickly spread to the other FAANG stocks—Apple, Amazon, Netflix, and Alphabet—which have also dropped since then. But the pain didn’t stop there. The Invesco QQQ ETF (QQQ), which tracks the 100 largest nonfinancial companies listed on Nasdaq, has also declined 4.2% from its its peak price of $182.82 through yesterday’s close.
That the Invesco QQQ ETF followed the FAANGs lower shouldn't be much of a surprise. The 120-day correlation between the five tech giants and the ETF hit an all-time high of 0.94 as on Monday. (A correlation of 1 means two assets move in lockstep.) That's high, considering that the FAANGs make up less than 40% of QQQ's holdings and the correlation between the two was only 0.65 three years ago.
The FAANGs make up just 12.8% of the S&P 500, but their impact has been felt even on that broader index. The correlation between the two has risen as high as 0.85 from just over 0.50 a few months ago. No wonder the market had a tough time continuing its rise following Facebook's drop.
The market might not be prepared for a FAANG flop. The five stocks have been rallying for a long time, and the latest fund manager survey from Bank of America Merrill Lynch noted that the "long FAANG" strategy remained the most-crowded trade for a sixth consecutive month.
But the tide might have started to turn. In a note last week, Michael Hartnett, chief investment strategist at Merrill Lynch, recommended investors short the FAANGs during the second half of 2018. But with the market and the FAANGs joined at the hip, it remains to be seen whether the Nasdaq and the S&P 500 can avoid tumbling too.
